Departmental News
Prof. J. Vince Ortiz Awarded Percy Julian Award
On Sept. 22, Prof. Ortiz received the 2026 Percy Julian Award from NoBCchE, the society’s highest honor. Click to read more about the award.
Prof. Lisa McElwee-White Elected ACS President!
Congratulations to Distinguished Professor Lisa McElwee-White, voted American Chemical Society President-Elect 2027!
Outreach Event: Harry Potter Potions
Chemistry Club volunteers created interactive Harry Potter-themed activities and chemistry demonstrations on Oct. 10, 2026 at the Millhopper Branch Library.
Outreach Event: Homecoming Tabling
Chemistry Club members organized an interactive slime-making demo during the Oct. 9 Homecoming Tabling event. Children, students, and adults learned about the principles of cross-linking and polymer chemistry in a fun and engaging experience.
UF Chemistry Hosts 2nd Annual Undergrad Research Symposium
UF Chemistry celebrated undergraduate research at its second annual symposium, featuring posters by over 60 students and a dozen award winners! The symposium showcased enthusiastic scientists and their cutting-edge scientific discoveries!

Recent Research
Austin Evans Wins NSF CAREER Award
Austin Evans receives one of the nation’s most prestigious honors for early-career faculty. This award will “explore new ways to use electricity to modify and break down plastics.” Click to read CLAS News article
Prof. George Christou Awarded the 2026 Charles H. Herty Medal of the ACS Southeastern Region
Congratulations to Distinguished Prof. George Christou, who was selected to receive the 2026 Charles H. Herty Medal!
UF Chemist Austin Evans Wins Prestigious Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Award
Congratulations to Prof. Austin Evans, who was selected of one of 17 new Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholars for 2026!
Narayanan Lab Receives ACS PRF Doctoral New Investigator Grant
Assistant Professor Amal Narayanan has received an American Chemical Society Petroleum Research Fund (ACS PRF) Doctoral New Investigator (DNI) grant to investigate surface properties of ultrahigh molecular weight polymers.
Loesgen Lab Discovers New Metabolites from Fungi
Anthracaurisin A, a novel compound with potent cytotoxic activity, was discovered from a Patagonian fungus. Read the Whitney Lab News post here.
